subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw support a cross-machine Chrome extension browser relay again, and if so should it be a vetted browser-backend plugin/API path rather than a restored core-only legacy driver?
rationale: The requested behavior is a shipped workflow regression, but the fix decides a browser-control security boundary and public driver/config/API contract that automation should not choose by simply re-adding the old enum and relay server.

options.title: Design a vetted plugin/API relay path
options.body: Add a versioned browser backend contract, security model, registered driver ids, docs, migration behavior, and an optional Chrome extension relay implementation after review.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Document that cross-machine browser control must use node host or remote CDP and close relay restoration requests once maintainers explicitly accept that product tradeoff.

options.title: Defer to narrower API work
options.body: Keep this issue open as user-impact evidence while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19289 settles the generic browser backend interface.

recommendation.title: Design a vetted plugin/API relay path
recommendation.body: Add a versioned browser backend contract, security model, registered driver ids, docs, migration behavior, and an optional Chrome extension relay implementation after review.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the clearest recent provenance for the relay removal and replacement driver migration that this decision would revisit.
